Hello!

I'd like to add the ~16.8Mgas limit from EIP-7825 to the agenda. This limit is a breaking change for application developers. While I appreciate the elegance of this constant in its RLP-encoded form, the fact that this limit is lower than the historical/conventional limit of 30M means that some dApps will break. I added some details at [Ethereum Magicians here](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7825-transaction-gas-limit-cap/21848/13). 

I really like the concept of EIP-7825, but the fact that this change is breaking at all is causing unnecessary work. It is a needless, _**unforced error**_ when the constant in this EIP could be higher with minimal-if-any impact. IMHO, EIPs affecting developer-visible features of Ethereum/the EVM should strive to avoid backwards incompatibility. Ethereum is a platform that demands immutability, so breaking things that cannot be patched is a major sin. Linus Torvalds is an asshole about not breaking Linux userspace, and we ought to strive for a similar (but perhaps less profanity-laden) stance towards smart contracts on the EVM.

Beyond the lack of elegance in the RLP-encoding of the gas limit, I don't see a compelling reason to set the limit lower and risk breaking things. I acknowledge that my vision is limited by my vantage point as an application-layer developer, so perhaps there is a compelling argument to the contrary.

Overall, 7825 is a great EIP and an important change to make, but I can't get behind ~16.8M as the limit

@duncancmt I emphasize with your stance, but I don't see the requirement to have 30MGas transactions on mainnet right now. It would be great if you could come up with a list of transactions/use-cases that necessitate the 30MGas cap so we can have a clear view of things that we will break with 7825

Hi! There are examples in the [Ethereum Magicians thread for 7987](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7987-transaction-gas-limit-cap-at-2-24/24746). This [example](https://github.com/mds1/convex-shutdown-simulation) of a system-critical transaction exceeding 16.8M gas seems particularly relevant. But my point really is the general one. At the risk of repeating myself: EIPs that break EVM apps are unacceptable. Don't break things in an ecosystem that demands immutability.

This is especially galling because the ~16.8M limit (rather than 30M) seems to have been a rather recent change. It's difficult for me as an application developer to keep up with the EIP/ACD process, and I don't think it's reasonable to expect feedback on the impact that a change like this will have on the ecosystem in that time frame.
@duncancmt I added your concern to the agenda, we can discuss it on the call but let's see if we can move the conversation forward on EthMag this week, too 😄
Even tho its an EL focused call, we need to discuss: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4477.  Same topic as "peerdas validator count concerns".

## Potential options for Fusaka upgrade dates 
Based on @timbeiko / @ralexstokes proposed timelines if we were able to upgrade prior to [Devconnect](https://devconnect.org/) (17-22 November)

* 15 or 22 Sep - Sepolia
* 16 Oct - Hoodi
* 15 Nov - Mainnet *15 November is a Saturday.  I assumed 12 November as last mid week date before Devconnect.

Also assume we want to do Holešky first.

**Proposed dates are potential options only, have not been agreed at ACD, are subject to change, including if issues arise in implementation/testing/security**

Data from upgrade scheduler: https://slots.symphonious.net/
Assuming mid week upgrades, if there were multiple options, preference given to Melbourne friendly times.
